summary: Through the Desert is a Knizia abstract where players snake colored camel trains across a hex desert, trying to reach oases and enclose territory while blocking rivals from doing the same. It plays fast and is easy to teach, but has real bite because routes can be sealed off with a single well-placed piece.
praised: elegant, easy-to-teach rules hiding real depth
tense spatial blocking reminiscent of Go
criticised: can feel visually and thematically dry
hidden scoring until the end can surprise new players
less satisfying at low player counts

interaction.detail: All camels are placed on a single shared board, and players directly cut off each other's expansion routes and race to claim oases and enclose empty territory, so almost the entire game state is shared and contested.

scoring.why: Points come from reaching oases, building the longest caravan line in each of five colors, enclosing empty desert regions, and small watering-hole bonus tiles, all kept hidden until the end.
scoring.how_you_win: Place camel pieces to build connected caravan routes that reach oases, try to have the longest line of each color, and enclose sections of empty desert; whoever's hidden score totals highest at the end wins.
